from itertools import product

options = {
    "A": "Confucius is very demanding in terms of diet.",
    "B": "Confucius lived in an era of both seasonal and out-of-season vegetables.",
    "C": "We can choose seasonal or out-of-season vegetables.",
    "D": "Diet not only nourishes the body, but also shapes the mind.",
}
submitted = "B"
print("Submitted option:", submitted, options[submitted])

# Test a literal reading:
# Knowledge about health and a prohibition on eating out-of-season
# vegetables do not themselves assert that such vegetables existed.
#
# Prohibition is represented as: if an out-of-season vegetable is
# available, Confucius does not eat it. This implication can hold
# even when none is available.
fields = (
    "knows_diet_and_health",
    "seasonal_available",
    "out_of_season_available",
    "eats_out_of_season",
)
models = []
for bits in product((False, True), repeat=len(fields)):
    world = dict(zip(fields, bits))
    physically_possible = (
        not world["eats_out_of_season"]
        or world["out_of_season_available"]
    )
    follows_prohibition = not world["eats_out_of_season"]
    premises = (
        world["knows_diet_and_health"]
        and physically_possible
        and follows_prohibition
    )
    if premises:
        models.append(world)

def option_b(world):
    return (
        world["seasonal_available"]
        and world["out_of_season_available"]
    )

countermodels = [world for world in models if not option_b(world)]
print("Literal-model enumeration: exhaustive, not sampled.")
print("Premise-satisfying worlds:", len(models))
print("Worlds in which B is false:", len(countermodels))
print("Counterexample:", countermodels[0])
print("Literal premises entail B:", not countermodels)

# A different, pragmatic interpretation treats the dietary instruction
# as presupposing an actual choice between both kinds of vegetables.
# Under that added presupposition, B follows, but the presupposition
# is not established by arithmetic or propositional enumeration.
contextual_models = [
    world for world in models
    if world["seasonal_available"] and world["out_of_season_available"]
]
print("With actual-choice presupposition, B follows:",
      bool(contextual_models) and all(map(option_b, contextual_models)))

print("UNSUPPORTED: The intended natural-language presupposition cannot "
      "be settled by this finite logical model. B requires a contextual "
      "reading; it is not entailed by the literal prohibition alone.")
print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
